correctness.rationale: Disjoint simple branch sets make the square classes independent; the tame degree-four cover has eight inertia-two branch fibers and genus five. Pullback and norm for the three involution quotients give the Jacobian product up to a power-of-two isogeny, preserving p-torsion for these odd primes. The two quartics have zero elliptic Cartier operators by the exponent test, so superspeciality (maximal a-number) reduces to zero Cartier on the genus-three quotient. In f^((p−1)/2) only x-exponents divisible by four occur; the three stated positions are all the possible nonzero entries. Independent replay python3 /workspace/reproductions/1.py (SymPy) computes the three gcds over the polynomial rings over the prime fields; the linear/quadratic factors give exactly the claimed geometric roots, not merely prime-field hits. Over F_31[u]/(u²+1), an independent norm-based quadratic character scan of all 961 affine x for each of the 29 parameters, including the degree-even monic fibers at infinity (four for C and two for each quotient), reproduced (1024,1024,1148,1272) exactly at 14,20,30 and no other maximal coefficient. Normalizing ordered branch triples to 0,1,infinity and comparing the resulting sets gave 16,8,8 stabilizer orders, zero maps from H_-1's branch set to H_14's and eight from H_14's to H_20's. All three sets have eight rational branch points over F_31², so the exhaustive triple comparison works geometrically. The reciprocal substitution also identifies the extra pair. No statement about distinct genus-five isomorphism classes is inferred.

value.rationale: This is a structured one-parameter arithmetic test case, with the canonical member and congruence class fixed before the search. Locating the first extra geometric roots, including showing absence outside the rational parameter sets at the three primes, gives exact classification data for the pencil. Distinguishing coefficient multiplicity from quotient isomorphism and identifying the displayed maximal models make those data usable without claiming a new general existence theorem, a new mechanism for maximality or a genus-five isomorphism classification.
